turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen learned about his zero from his phone in the middle of a class and nobody called me first, so start with who decided that, and when.
Thanks for coming in. The zero went in before I called you, and that was wrong.
Okay. Now tell me on what basis you gave it, because if the answer is a piece of software, we're going upstairs.
I will remove the zero tomorrow morning. Owen does a private supervised rewrite at lunch on Thursday. Nothing goes on his record. I will put all of that in an email to you tonight.
I'm writing that down: the zero removed tomorrow morning, nothing on his record, and an email tonight. What I haven't heard is why Owen should rewrite an essay he already wrote. On what basis, Hale?
Yes, all of it, in writing tonight.
That doesn't answer my question. If you're asking him to redo his work, you have a reason, so show me what you have or the rewrite comes off the table with the zero.
Okay, I think that is the end of the meeting. Thank you.

We're not done, Hale. You've agreed to remove the zero tomorrow morning and keep this off his record, but you haven't told me why Owen sits a rewrite on Thursday. Until you show me something, my position is that the zero comes off and there is no rewrite.
